name: Dan Sullivan
role: U.S. senator from Alaska (2015–present), former Alaska attorney general and natural resources commissioner
summary: Sullivan promotes Alaska resource development, military strength and stricter border enforcement, alongside targeted public investment and healthcare funding. He favours state authority in selected social policies, opposes most abortions, and supported federal marriage recognition with religious exemptions.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Argues that growth and individual ingenuity are stifled when government dictates the boundaries of success and that regulation of every aspect of business holds opportunity back.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: His 2025 presentation says he supported raising the top rate from 37 to 39.6 percent for incomes above $25 million, a limited increase.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He urged regulation of prescription-drug middlemen while campaigning to ease energy permitting. His position varies by sector.

cut-welfare.rationale: He defended a targeted safety net and Alaska health funding while requiring work and tighter benefit administration. This is selective reform, not wholesale rejection.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Did not support Alaska's 2014 marijuana legalisation, though he now defends the state's right to regulate it, and campaigns against fentanyl.

strong-leader.rationale: Condemned President Obama's and President Biden's unilateral orders as overreach (vaccine mandate, Bering Sea order) yet welcomed President Trump's sweeping executive order on Alaska.

state-harmful.rationale: Treats government as a partner in opportunity and in national defence, wanting it less of an obstacle, not unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: He opposed the 2022 gun-control bill and pledged to resist legislation infringing the right to bear arms.

empower-police-military.rationale: He promoted major military and Coast Guard expansion alongside greater support for law enforcement.

decide-locally.rationale: He explicitly supported state authority over marijuana regulation and abortion decisions, rather than uniform federal control.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: His later vote protected recognition of valid same-sex marriages; he stressed religious safeguards and acknowledged earlier opposition to Obergefell. Support is qualified.

abortion-legal.rationale: His documented policy opposed most abortions with specified exceptions; he later backed Dobbs and reiterated his anti-abortion commitment.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Offered an amendment to bar U.S. funding to the UN Human Rights Council and urged the Secretary of State not to take the Iran deal to the UN first.

free-trade.rationale: Voted for and praised Trade Promotion Authority, saying such trade agreements work when negotiated correctly and open export markets, in a statement from 2015.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Commended the 2017 and 2018 strikes on Syria's chemical-weapons capability as a response to attacks on civilians.

open-borders.rationale: He supported border-wall funding and stronger enforcement; the evidence addresses present border policy rather than a distant borderless ideal.

limit-growth.rationale: His energy plan insists on growth and employment while rejecting shutdowns of productive industries for climate policy.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: His plan accepts emissions reduction but rejects sweeping economic restructuring and mandates based on catastrophic projections. It favours technology and market-led measures.

expand-nuclear.rationale: His jointly authored energy plan calls for expanding the nuclear fleet, including advanced and small modular reactors.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He sought federal Energy Department financing for Alaska LNG and promoted military-based AI infrastructure.

one-party-rule.rationale: Calls the elections of Russia, Iran and China shams and attacks Xi's one-man rule in perpetuity by crushing dissent.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said after the attempt on President Trump that political violence is abhorrent and has absolutely no place in the country.

military-superiority.rationale: Campaigns for peace through strength, a most lethal force, more shipbuilding and defence spending above 3 percent of GDP.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Calls Israel the Jewish homeland and the Middle East's only democracy and defends its existence and right to self-defence.

national-self-determination.rationale: Backs Taiwan's free elections and Ukraine's democracy against Chinese and Russian coercion.

work-for-welfare.rationale: He explicitly defended work requirements for able-bodied beneficiaries, with exemptions and Alaska flexibility.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: His 2026 address championed new oil leases, increased production and the Alaska LNG pipeline.

national-mission.rationale: Endorses Reagan's call to be shy no longer in promoting democracy and calls liberty America's most powerful weapon, as chairman of the International Republican Institute.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Calls in his maiden speech for federal infrastructure and job legislation and wants Washington to be a partner in progress, so he does not limit government to defence and courts.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Speaks in his own voice of true equality under 'all men are created equal' among people of different races and creeds.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He accepted the electorate’s removal of Trump and said voters should decide whether he could hold future office.

separated-powers.rationale: He explicitly identified separation of powers as a constitutional value central to his judicial-selection criteria.

party-controls-media.rationale: Introduced the INFORM Act to bypass the CCP's censorship apparatus and support independent journalism.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He urged strengthening NATO, increasing allied commitments and maintaining effective military cooperation.

religious-exemptions.rationale: He explicitly championed protections for churches and religious universities adhering to traditional marriage.

collective-defense.rationale: Calls the U.S. commitment to European security ironclad and defends NATO's long-term health.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He treated the constitutional right to bear arms as a binding limit on legislation.

non-intervention.rationale: He supported attacks on Iran and said the United States could shape regime change, while leaving Iran’s political outcome to its people.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: He celebrated increasing Alaska’s share of federal-land resource revenue to 70 percent.

defeat-communism.rationale: Praises Reagan's strategy that helped bring down Soviet communism and urges exploiting the CCP's fear of its own people.

suppress-opposition.rationale: After condemning January 6 violence, he insisted that peaceful Trump supporters retain their political voice and expression.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: He signed a letter opposing treatment of gender identity as sex under Title IX, particularly in schools and athletics. This concerns that legal context.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Calls for a more lethal force and larger defence budgets to deter war.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: His signed letter explicitly describes sex as biological, binary and grounded in immutable reproductive characteristics.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Supports strikes on Syria and Iran to deter chemical weapons and a nuclear programme, beyond defending against an attack on the U.S.

pollution-taxes.rationale: He promoted a ten-year methane-tax moratorium, opposing this particular pollution levy.

close-ties-china.rationale: Describes Xi and the CCP as a dictatorship pursuing aggression and sponsors sanctions, investment limits and Taiwan legislation against China.

notes:
Living-person answers use documented positions, never party-based inference. Latest clear evidence is preferred: marriage recognition is qualified, and his support for a limited top-income tax increase is retained. Marijuana federalism is not legalisation of all recreational drugs. Medicaid support and criticism of Obamacare do not establish a position on universal healthcare as such. Support for military force is not automatically support for intervention for humanitarian reasons. Opposition to sentence reductions does not by itself establish a general view of prison rehabilitation. His relatives’ ancestry and third-party praise do not establish an Indigenous land-authority position. Direct downloads of Senate pages and PDFs were attempted but returned access denials; full browser-accessible texts were reviewed. All 490 statements were checked against the research.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 21 answers taken from it, 15 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass from his own press releases, floor speeches, letters and interviews on sullivan.senate.gov (the site returns 403 to direct requests, so pages were read from Internet Archive captures of the same URLs). Themes searched: economy, government, society, world, liberty, ecology, technology, means. Nothing found on healthcare, welfare, taxes on the wealthy, unions, wages, trade tariffs in 2025, courts beyond judicial restraint, elections law, term limits, or the filibuster. Marriage is 0 low: he disagrees with Obergefell yet voted for the Respect for Marriage Act. Votes alone (Ukraine aid HR 7691 yea, 2022) were not used to answer any statement.
